Reflection: true is cytochalasin D, annotated Actin disruptors; I concluded Eg5 inhibitors (p=0.45), incorrect.

What I missed: massive actin texture/heterogeneity (act_std z+179/+67, act_glcm_contrast z+138/+50, act_mean up) plus rounding/retraction fibers and cortical rims were the direct actin-disruptor signal. I misread bright condensed DNA + frac_mitotic_like (z 91/20) + tub_mean increase as mitotic-arrest stabilizer/Eg5, but tubulin brightening was largely geometric concentration in rounded cells, as the microscopist cautioned. Atlas was actually pointing correctly: combined wells had actin disruptors cytochalasin B and latrunculin B at sim 0.90/0.80; mid-dose alone had cytochalasin B at 0.905.

Literature confirms: cytochalasin D caps/severs actin filaments and blocks polymerization (PMID:3023337, PMID:40658853), incl. via actin-cofilin inhibition (PMID:22728040).

Lesson: when actin texture dominates plus rounding without resolvable bipolar/monopolar spindles, keep Actin disruptors on top despite mitotic-like classifier firing, and weight atlas actin neighbours more. Requested dose5 rep2 could not be acquired - budget spent.

reflection.text:
High-dose well w_bdc02a8567 showed extreme texture signals in both channels (tub_glcm_contrast z=+185.2, act_std z=+179.3) with low cell counts, and mid-dose w_b617e84d8d retained strong act_std z=+66.9, so I correctly sensed a potent cytoskeletal phenotype persistent from 0.3-10 uM but framed rounding and bright condensed signal as mitotic arrest favoring Microtubule stabilizers then Eg5 inhibitors.
The error was treating increased tubulin intensity/texture as stabilized polymer while discounting that actin-network collapse and rounding geometrically condenses tubulin/DNA signal and inflates contrast; I down-weighted Actin disruptors to 0.10 then 0.08 despite the largest actin-channel z-scores and despite atlas hits of Actin disruptors 3/10 in e6 and e13, because microscopist descriptions in e4/e5 listed only stabilizer/Eg5.
With only two wells acquired all dose_response calls in e8-e11 were inconclusive, and after the review I switched to Eg5 on per-well atlas majority in e14 without new data instead of holding actin as a live mimic of mitotic arrest; actin disruption should have remained co-equal given dual-channel texture changes.

Reference atlas did surface Actin disruptors at 3/10 in e6 and e13 alongside Eg5, preserving the true class as a neighbor that should have been pursued

Discounted Actin disruptors from 0.10 to 0.08 despite act_std z=+179.3 and act_glcm_contrast z=+138.0 because visual candidates in e4/e5 omitted actin

Acquired only 10 uM and 0.3 uM single replicates leaving dose_response for tub_mean, frac_mitotic_like and cell_count inconclusive, then changed final call from stabilizer to Eg5 on per-well atlas counts in e13-e14 with no new well data

## Hypothesis history

- after step 7: Microtubule stabilizers 0.55, Eg5 inhibitors 0.25, Actin disruptors 0.10, Cholesterol-lowering 0.10
- after step 15: Eg5 inhibitors 0.45, Microtubule stabilizers 0.30, Cholesterol-lowering 0.10, Actin disruptors 0.08, Microtubule destabilizers 0.07

## Conclusion 1

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e5.

Why: Rounded mitotic arrest with bright condensed DNA and increased tubulin mass favors stabilized polymer over loss or Eg5 rosettes.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution spindle immunofluorescence (tubulin + pericentrin/DAPI) to score bipolar stabilized bundles vs monopolar Eg5 rosettes vs multipolar Aurora, plus tubulin polymerization assay.

## Conclusion 2

**Eg5 inhibitors** (stated probability 0.45); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e6, e14.

Why: Cannot acquire dose5 rep2, budget spent. Mitotic rounding persists 0.3-10uM but per-well atlas shows no stabilizer, Eg5 majority; tubulin bright partly geometric so switch top to Eg5.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Cannot acquire dose5 rep2: budget spent. Next: high-resolution tubulin/pericentrin/DAPI spindle imaging to score monopolar Eg5 rosettes vs stabilized bundles, plus in vitro tubulin polymerization assay.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Not justified: two doses support mitotic arrest, but atlas nearest neighbours contain no microtubule stabilizer and favour Eg5/actin/cholesterol; tubulin brightness is partly geometric, so 0.62 is slightly over-weighted. However every key result is single-replicate and dose-responses were explicitly inconclusive.

Requested: Acquire dose 5 (1.0 µM) replicate 2 to provide a third independent point that completes the dose-response trend for tub_mean/frac_mitotic_like and checks whether the stabilizer signal persists at an intermediate dose or collapses toward the atlas profile.

## Unblinding

Compound: **cytochalasin D** (PubChem CID [5458428](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5458428))

Identity check: name only (the BBBC021 structure is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Eg5 inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

High-dose well w_bdc02a8567 showed extreme texture signals in both channels (tub_glcm_contrast z=+185.2, act_std z=+179.3) with low cell counts, and mid-dose w_b617e84d8d retained strong act_std z=+66.9, so I correctly sensed a potent cytoskeletal phenotype persistent from 0.3-10 uM but framed rounding and bright condensed signal as mitotic arrest favoring Microtubule stabilizers then Eg5 inhibitors.
The error was treating increased tubulin intensity/texture as stabilized polymer while discounting that actin-network collapse and rounding geometrically condenses tubulin/DNA signal and inflates contrast; I down-weighted Actin disruptors to 0.10 then 0.08 despite the largest actin-channel z-scores and despite atlas hits of Actin disruptors 3/10 in e6 and e13, because microscopist descriptions in e4/e5 listed only stabilizer/Eg5.
With only two wells acquired all dose_response calls in e8-e11 were inconclusive, and after the review I switched to Eg5 on per-well atlas majority in e14 without new data instead of holding actin as a live mimic of mitotic arrest; actin disruption should have remained co-equal given dual-channel texture changes.

What was right:
- Detected a strong, dose-persistent cytoskeletal disruption with reduced density and very large texture z-scores in both actin and tubulin channels, correctly excluding inactive/weak phenotypes
- Reference atlas did surface Actin disruptors at 3/10 in e6 and e13 alongside Eg5, preserving the true class as a neighbor that should have been pursued
- Review critique was correct that tubulin brightness was partly geometric and that 0.62 for Microtubule stabilizers was over-weighted on single-replicate wells with inconclusive dose trends

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread tub_glcm_contrast z=+185.2 and bright condensed DNA as increased tubulin mass/stabilization rather than contraction/rounding secondary to F-actin loss
- Discounted Actin disruptors from 0.10 to 0.08 despite act_std z=+179.3 and act_glcm_contrast z=+138.0 because visual candidates in e4/e5 omitted actin
- Acquired only 10 uM and 0.3 uM single replicates leaving dose_response for tub_mean, frac_mitotic_like and cell_count inconclusive, then changed final call from stabilizer to Eg5 on per-well atlas counts in e13-e14 with no new well data

Proposed next experiment: Parallel phalloidin F-actin + tubulin + DAPI high-resolution imaging across 0.03-10 uM with replicates to score loss of stress fibers, cell rounding/contraction, cytokinesis failure/binucleation and spindle bipolarity, plus cell-free actin polymerization/barbed-end capping assay to directly test actin vs tubulin mechanism.

## Citations

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [3023337](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3023337/): Actin polymerization. The mechanism of action of cytochalasin D. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D blocks actin polymerization by capping the barbed end of filaments
- PMID [40658853](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40658853/): Microscopic and structural observations of actin filament capping and severing by cytochalasin D. *Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A* (2025) — Recent structural work confirms cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments
- PMID [3782101](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3782101/): The kinetics of cytochalasin D binding to monomeric actin. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D binds monomeric actin and alters assembly kinetics
- PMID [22728040](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22728040/): Cytochalasin D acts as an inhibitor of the actin-cofilin interaction. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun* (2012) — Cytochalasin D also inhibits the actin-cofilin interaction, perturbing turnover
